name: Centro Historico (Praca Tiradentes)
tagline: Baroque heart around the main square
description: The historic centre around Praca Tiradentes is Ouro Preto's UNESCO-listed core, packed with baroque churches, museums, cobbled hills, pousadas, restaurants and shops. It is the most walkable and amenity-rich base, though its steep slopes demand strong legs.
bestFor: Travellers wanting sights, dining and pousadas within walking distance

name: Antonio Dias
description: Antonio Dias is a historic eastern district built around the Matriz de Nossa Senhora da Conceicao church, where the sculptor Aleijadinho is buried. Quieter and steeply set, it offers traditional colonial houses and a more residential, local atmosphere close to the centre.
bestFor: Visitors wanting historic character away from the busiest square

name: Pilar (Nossa Senhora do Pilar)
description: The Pilar district surrounds the Basilica of Nossa Senhora do Pilar, one of Brazil's most gilded baroque churches. This western historic parish blends colonial houses, student housing linked to the university, and quiet cobbled streets a short walk from the centre.
bestFor: Longer-stay visitors wanting heritage streets and student-town energy

name: Sao Cristovao
description: Sao Cristovao is a largely residential neighbourhood on the hills surrounding the historic core. It offers more affordable long-stay rooms and apartments, local shops and quieter streets, with sweeping views over the town's rooftops and church towers below.
bestFor: Budget and long-stay visitors wanting local life and town views
